authority_basis.claim_scope: Zero net force implies zero acceleration in an inertial frame, not necessarily zero velocity.

concepts.statement: Mechanical equilibrium means zero acceleration because the net external force is zero; velocity may be nonzero and constant.
concepts.why_required: It separates zero acceleration from zero velocity and anchors Newtonian equilibrium in net external force.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Learners may conclude that balanced forces imply rest or that equilibrium means no forces act.

model_conditions.condition: The analysis is performed in an inertial reference frame.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Newton's first-law equilibrium statement does not include pseudo-forces from an accelerating frame.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Apparent acceleration can occur despite zero modelled real-force sum unless inertial corrections are included.

representations.semantic_geometry: A selected-system FBD shows balanced external force vectors while motion state is represented separately from force balance.
representations.verification_method: Vector-sum the FBD forces and distinguish the resulting acceleration statement from the current velocity state.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Use the selected-system FBD to determine the vector net external force.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Equilibrium may be asserted without accounting for all external forces.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: If the net external force is zero, conclude the acceleration is zero in the inertial frame.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Zero force balance may be confused with zero motion.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Keep constant nonzero velocity as a valid equilibrium motion state unless another condition fixes the velocity.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The learner may force equilibrium objects to be at rest.

required_transformations.description: Translate a complete FBD into the vector net-force statement without collapsing it to a motion claim.
Infer zero acceleration while preserving both rest and constant nonzero velocity as possible states.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Equilibrium means no forces act or the object must be at rest.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Many introductory examples use stationary objects with balanced forces, conflating one motion state with the general condition.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A puck moving at constant velocity on an ideal frictionless surface has zero acceleration without being at rest.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Pair a balanced FBD with a separate velocity arrow that remains nonzero and constant.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Equilibrium requires vector cancellation of forces and zero acceleration, not absence of forces or zero velocity.
misconceptions.verification: Check that the net force is zero and that any constant velocity is compatible with a=0.

problem_families.name: Mechanical equilibrium and constant-velocity dynamics
problem_families.first_technical_move: Construct the FBD and evaluate the net external force before interpreting the motion state.
fatal_errors: setting velocity to zero because net force is zero

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove the zero-net-force does not imply zero-velocity invariant.
